key_insight: Off-the-shelf large language models can automatically extract key breast oncology variables from very long longitudinal charts with high agreement to expert abstraction for many outcomes.
clinical_relevance: This could greatly reduce the manual workload of chart review in oncology research, especially for retrospective studies where important details are buried in narrative notes.
method: Randomly sampled 100 patients from a complex institutional breast cancer cohort.
Compared four general-purpose LLMs against oncologist abstraction, genetic testing records, and select research coordinator abstraction.
Built an open-source HIPAA-compliant pipeline without fine-tuning or hand-selecting input documents.
evidence_signal: The best models (GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro) reached 90%–100% concordance for several variables, and performance on recurrence detection was similar in a separate cohort of 97 patients.
watch_item: Results may not generalize across institutions, disease settings, or record structures, so external validation is needed before broad deployment.
paper_title: Fully Automated Abstraction of Longitudinal Breast Oncology Records with Off-The-Shelf Large Language Models
